content: 1. If a dry shipper or an overpack is used for the transportation of infectious substances, this must be explicitly indicated, along with the type and quantity of the individual packages contained within. 2. Handling requirements for the carrier must be clearly specified. These include any necessary actions such as loading, stowing, or unloading. If no special handling is required, a statement indicating No such requirements are necessary should be provided. 3. Any restrictions on the mode of transportation that can or must be used should be outlined. Regardless of the routing, the transport must be conducted via the quickest possible route. If transshipment is necessary, precautions must be taken to ensure special care, expedited handling, and monitoring of the substance during transit. 4. Emergency arrangements applicable to the package must be included. 5. For Category A infectious substances, the name and telephone number of a responsible person must be marked on the package(s) and on the shipper’s declaration in the additional handling information section. For Category B infectious substances (UN 3373), the name and telephone number of a responsible person must be provided on the air waybill or on the package. 6. Emergency response information must be immediately available for carriers to use in the event of accidents or incidents involving infectious substances during transport. 7. A shipper’s declaration must include a signed and dated statement acknowledging that the package has been prepared in accordance with applicable requirements. Only trained personnel are authorized to complete and sign the shipper’s declaration. 8. An air waybill must accompany all shipments of infectious substances, even if a Dangerous Goods Transport Document (DGTD) has already been completed. The air waybill should include the shipper’s and receiver’s names and addresses, carrier information, and details about the quantities and types of packages. 9. For Category A infectious substances, the air waybill must include the statement Dangerous Goods as per associated Shipper’s Declaration. For Category B infectious substances, the name and telephone number of a responsible person must be included on the air waybill or package. 10. If the shipment includes dry ice, the UN number, proper shipping name, and net quantity of dry ice must also be provided. 11. A contractual arrangement between the shipper and receiver is essential for the safe and secure transportation of infectious substances. This agreement should outline the responsibilities and obligations of both parties and may be regulated through a Material Transfer Agreement (MTA) or mutually agreed terms (MAT). 12. An MTA is a legal contract governing the transfer of materials, such as infectious substances, between two parties. It defines the terms and conditions of the transfer, including restrictions on use, handling, or disposal, and ensures compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. 13. In the event of a spill involving infectious substances, trained personnel should follow a specific clean-up procedure. This includes wearing protective clothing, covering the spill with absorbent material, applying disinfectant, and safely disposing of contaminated materials. The incident must be reported to the competent authority after successful decontamination. 14. Reporting mechanisms for accidents and incidents involving dangerous goods must be established by relevant national and international organizations. These mechanisms ensure timely and adequate responses to minimize risks and manage the situation effectively. 15. Shippers must comply with legal requirements, including reporting, compliance checks, and potential penalties. Findings from investigations should inform protocol reviews and adjustments to prevent recurrence. 16. Failure to comply with international conventions, treaties, and regulations can result in significant penalties and legal consequences, as well as hinder the transportation of infectious substances. 17. The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) is an international treaty aimed at conserving and sustainably using biological diversity. Compliance with such conventions is essential to ensure the safe and secure transport of infectious substances and to promote the sustainable use of genetic resources.
